frequency_question: What proportion of standalone, highly partisan federal election integrity bills pass the U.S. Senate within a single Congress (approx. 2-year window)?
membership_rule: Includes major standalone federal legislation targeting voter eligibility, registration, or election administration that lack bipartisan sponsorship and reach the Senate floor or are explicitly brought to a vote. Excludes provisions bundled into omnibus appropriations bills or must-pass defense authorizations.

cases.name: Help America Vote Act (HAVA) amendments / standalone partisan integrity bills (2005)
Freedom to Vote Act / John Lewis Voting Rights Advancement Act (2022)
American Confidence in Elections (ACE) Act / Senate companion counterparts

provenance_note: rate of 0% from only 4 case(s); too few to establish an extreme base rate -- treat as directional
coverage_note: 4 major named legislative pushes identified where strict partisan voting bills were pursued; none passed the Senate as standalone measures.
known_gaps: Minor technical amendments to existing election laws are excluded; focus is strictly on major contested eligibility/registration bills.
skeleton: Partisan federal election reform initiatives introduced in the Senate over the past 6 congressional sessions (2013-2024), partitioned into bills requiring documentary proof of citizenship vs general administrative changes.
multiplier: 4 distinct legislative pushes for major partisan electoral changes resulting in 0 Senate passages due to filibuster thresholds (60-vote requirement).
validity_reason: Valid until the expiration of the current Senate procedural rules (specifically the 60-vote filibuster threshold for legislation).
